title: 月下独酌·其一
titlePy: Yuè Xià Dú Zhuó · Qí Yī
author: 李白
intro: Alone among the flowers with a jug of wine, Li Bai invites the moon and his own shadow to drink with him — and turns loneliness into a party of three. One of the most playful poems in Chinese.
analysis: 诗人在花丛中独自喝酒，身边没有一个亲近的人。他忽然想出一个办法：举起酒杯请月亮来，再加上地上自己的影子，正好“对影成三人”。可是月亮不会喝酒，影子也只会跟着他，这份热闹其实是假的。他并不在意，干脆趁着春光及时行乐：他唱歌，月亮好像在徘徊倾听；他跳舞，影子跟着乱晃。清醒时三个“朋友”一起高兴，喝醉了就各自散去。最后他和月亮、影子约定，要在遥远的银河再相会。全诗用了拟人的手法——把月亮和影子当成人来写，越写得热闹，越让人感到诗人的孤独；但他的孤独不是悲伤的，而是潇洒、浪漫的，这正是李白的风格。
analysisEn: Li Bai sits among the flowers with a jug of wine and nobody to share it. So he invents company: he raises his cup to invite the moon, and with his shadow on the ground, “we make three.” Then he admits the joke — the moon can’t drink, and the shadow only follows him around. It doesn’t stop him. While spring lasts, he will enjoy it: when he sings, the moon seems to linger and listen; when he dances, his shadow staggers along. Sober, the three of them have a fine time; drunk, they drift apart. At the end he makes a promise to these companions “without feelings”: to meet again far away, in the River of Stars. The poem works through personification — treating the moon and the shadow as if they were people. The livelier the little party sounds, the more we feel how alone he really is. Yet the loneliness is not gloomy. It is free, a little wild and full of imagination — exactly what readers love in Li Bai.
background: Li Bai (701–762), the “Immortal of Poetry”, was famous for his love of wine and the moon. This is the first of four poems with the same title, usually dated to around 744 in Chang’an, when his hopes at the imperial court were fading.
pronunciation: 暂伴月将影：将 jiāng，意思是“和、与”，不读 jiàng。行乐：xíng lè。相期：xiāng qī。邈 miǎo（遥远）。醉后各分散：散 sàn。
version: 采用通行的教材及选本文本。“我舞影零乱”的“零乱”一作“凌乱”；“醒时同交欢”一作“醒时相交欢”。原题共四首，此为第一首。

lines.lit: Among the flowers, a jug of wine;
lines.en: A jug of wine among the flowers,

lines.lit: pouring alone, no one close to me.
lines.en: I pour alone, no friend in sight.

lines.lit: Raising my cup, I invite the bright moon;
lines.en: I lift my cup and ask the moon to join me —

lines.lit: facing my shadow, we become three people.
lines.en: with my shadow, that makes three.

lines.lit: The moon, after all, does not know how to drink;
lines.en: But the moon has never learned to drink,

lines.lit: the shadow merely follows my body.
lines.en: and my shadow only trails behind me.

lines.lit: For now I keep company with the moon and the shadow;
lines.en: Still, for now, moon and shadow will do for friends:

lines.lit: seeking joy must be done while it is spring.
lines.en: joy must be caught while spring is here.

lines.lit: I sing, and the moon lingers back and forth;
lines.en: I sing — the moon stays, wavering, to listen;

lines.lit: I dance, and the shadow scatters in disorder.
lines.en: I dance — my shadow tumbles all around.

lines.lit: When sober, we share our joy together;
lines.en: While I’m sober, we’re merry together;

lines.lit: after getting drunk, each goes his own way.
lines.en: once I’m drunk, we each wander off.

lines.lit: Forever we bind a friendship free of worldly feeling;
lines.en: Let us be friends for good, beyond all human ties,

lines.lit: we promise to meet in the distant River of Stars.
lines.en: and meet again far off, in the River of Stars.

words.note: 古义；现代汉语多用在“斟酌”（仔细考虑）里。
书面语，现代汉语说“一个人喝酒”。
古义是“亲近的人”；今天的“相亲”指男女经人介绍见面，意思完全不同。
古义“不懂得、不会”；今天“不解”多指“不理解”。
现代汉语“徒劳”“徒然”里还有这个意思。
古义“和、与”；今天的“将”多表示“将要”。

words.en: to seek pleasure; to enjoy oneself
words.note: 今天成语“及时行乐”还在用。

words.en: to pace back and forth; to linger

words.note: 现代汉语也说，常写作“凌乱”。
指和没有感情的月亮、影子交朋友，不是“无情无义”。
书面语，现代汉语说“约好见面”。
生僻字，现代汉语说“遥远”。

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月亮被请来当酒友，是诗人想象出的伙伴，越热闹越显出他的孤独。
imagery.en: The moon is invited as a drinking companion — an imaginary friend whose presence only shows how alone he is.

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 酒是孤独的陪伴，也让诗人放开自己，唱歌跳舞、及时行乐。
imagery.en: Wine keeps him company and sets him free to sing, dance and enjoy the moment.

imagery.name: 花
imagery.zh: 花丛写出春夜的美好，美景当前却无人同赏，更添寂寞。
imagery.en: The flowers make the spring night lovely — but beauty with no one to share it only deepens the loneliness.
